# Best Broadway Shows from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway shows that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of a theatrical season cut dramatically short. These productions, which debuted in the brief window before the industry's historic shutdown, continue to resonate with audiences and critics alike.

Leading our selection is **Les Misérables**, which earns an 83/100 score for its grittier, reimagined production at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre. This isn't your traditional staging of the beloved musical—the production takes a darker, more visceral approach that has won over most critics, though some purists remain unconvinced by the radical departure from the original.

**A Soldier's Play** stands as another critical highlight, scoring 78/100 across 29 reviews. Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama finally made its long-overdue Broadway debut in a stellar revival that proves the work's examination of race, power, and identity remains urgently relevant. The production demonstrates how classic American plays can speak powerfully across decades.

The season also includes **Grand Horizons**, a more traditional boulevard comedy featuring acclaimed performances from Jane Alexander and James Cromwell, alongside Laura Linney's divisive but technically impressive solo turn in **My Name is Lucy Barton**. Rounding out our selection is Ivo van Hove's polarizing **West Side Story** reimagining, which splits critics between those embracing its bold vision and those mourning the loss of traditional staging.

With an average critic score of 75/100, these five productions showcase the range of theatrical ambition that defined early 2020. Whether you're drawn to experimental reinventions or more conventional storytelling, this guide will help you discover which of these historically significant shows deserves your attention.

best-broadway-shows-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows from 2021

As we reach March 2026, the Broadway productions that opened in 2021 continue to demonstrate remarkable staying power, representing a pivotal moment when theater returned from its pandemic shutdown. These ten shows, averaging an impressive 81/100 critical score, capture both the industry's resilience and its artistic ambition during an unprecedented period of reopening.

The year's offerings span an unusually wide artistic spectrum. Experimental works like **Dana H.** push theatrical boundaries with Deirdre O'Connell's mesmerizing lip-sync performance in this unconventional docudrama, earning the highest critical acclaim at 86/100. Meanwhile, **The Phantom of the Opera** proves that Broadway's traditional mega-musicals retain their spectacular appeal, with Lloyd Webber's enduring score and production values still captivating audiences despite—or perhaps because of—their unabashed theatricality.

The 2021 season also marked Broadway's conscious reckoning with representation and relevance. **Pass Over** earned particular significance as the first play to reopen Broadway, blending Beckett and Exodus to examine Black American experience with urgent power. Solo performances flourished as well, with Ruben Santiago-Hudson's **Lackawanna Blues** and Tala Ashe's **Is This a Room** demonstrating how single actors can command Broadway stages with verbatim texts and deeply personal stories.

Classic revivals received bold reimaginings: **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club** transforms its venue into an immersive experience, while **Company** revitalizes Sondheim's masterwork through gender-swapping that critics largely celebrate as vital rather than gimmicky. From Lynn Nottage's compassionate **Clyde's** to the pop-powered **SIX**, these productions reflect a theater industry emerging from crisis with both artistic daring and crowd-pleasing confidence.

Whether you're drawn to experimental theater or traditional spectacle, these enduring productions offer compelling reasons to experience what made 2021 a watershed year for Broadway.

# Best Broadway Plays from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theater interrupted—a season cut dramatically short by the pandemic, yet one that managed to deliver several productions that have endured in cultural memory.

Leading our rankings is the reimagined **Les Misérables** at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre, earning an 83/100 from critics who largely embraced its grittier approach to the classic material, even as some found the radical reworking less emotionally resonant than traditional stagings. Close behind, **A Soldier's Play** stands as one of the season's most significant achievements—Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama finally received its long-overdue Broadway debut in a stellar revival that proved the play's examination of race, power, and military justice remains urgently relevant decades after its creation.

The season's other offerings showcase Broadway's range, from **Grand Horizons**, a well-crafted boulevard comedy elevated by powerhouse performances from Jane Alexander and James Cromwell, to more divisive experiments like Ivo van Hove's radical **West Side Story** reimagining, which polarized critics with its bold visual approach and contemporary staging choices. Laura Linney's solo turn in **My Name is Lucy Barton** similarly divided opinion, with unanimous praise for her luminous performance tempered by questions about the adaptation's theatrical viability.

With an average critical score of 75/100 across these five productions, the 2020 season—though abbreviated—demonstrated Broadway's ongoing commitment to both honoring classic works and championing important voices that had been previously overlooked. Explore our detailed reviews below to discover which of these productions might still resonate with your theatrical interests.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that debuted in 2021 represent a watershed moment for American theater. That year marked not only the industry's return from its pandemic shutdown but also a remarkable creative flourishing, with productions that pushed theatrical boundaries and redefined what Broadway could be.

The standout achievement remains **Dana H.**, Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama featuring Deirdre O'Connell's mesmerizing lip-sync performance to a real interview with Hnath's mother about her kidnapping. Critics continue to hail it as one of the most innovative theatrical experiments to reach Broadway. Equally experimental is **Is This a Room**, which transforms a verbatim FBI transcript of Reality Winner's interrogation into gripping, pulse-pounding theater that proves documentary theater can be as thrilling as any fictional drama.

The year also saw the return of spectacle with **The Phantom of the Opera** continuing its historic run, alongside ambitious new productions like **The Lehman Trilogy**, Sam Mendes's epic examination of capitalism and the American dream told through 150 years of one family's story. Meanwhile, **Pass Over** earned its place in history as Broadway's first play to reopen after the shutdown, with Antoinette Chinonye Nwandu's urgent drama blending Beckett and biblical themes to examine Black American experience.

The ten plays featured here average an impressive 81/100 critic score, spanning from intimate solo performances to immersive theatrical reimaginings like **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club**. Whether you're discovering these productions for the first time or revisiting old favorites, this collection represents a pivotal chapter in Broadway history worth exploring.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays from 2022

As of March 2026, the class of 2022 stands as one of Broadway's most critically acclaimed seasons in recent memory, with an impressive average critic score of 83/100 across our top ten productions. This remarkable year brought a diverse array of voices to the stage, from bold new works to essential revivals that redefined classic texts for contemporary audiences.

Leading the pack is **Kimberly Akimbo**, the quirky musical that critics continue to celebrate as a near-perfect achievement, deftly balancing laugh-out-loud comedy with profound emotional depth. Close behind, **Into the Woods** offers a stripped-down revival that serves as a triumphant tribute to Stephen Sondheim, while **A Strange Loop**—Michael R. Jackson's Pulitzer Prize-winning meta-musical—pushes boundaries with its brazenly original exploration of identity and self-perception.

The 2022 season proves particularly notable for its celebration of Pulitzer Prize-winning works, with five of our featured productions carrying this distinction. From Tom Stoppard's deeply personal **Leopoldstadt**, a haunting meditation on Jewish identity and the Holocaust, to revivals of Suzan-Lori Parks' **Topdog/Underdog** and Paula Vogel's **How I Learned to Drive**, the year demonstrated Broadway's commitment to presenting challenging, essential drama alongside innovative new voices.

The range extends from Mike Birbiglia's masterful solo storytelling in **The Old Man & The Pool** to Jordan E. Cooper's audacious satire **Ain't No Mo'**, proving that 2022 offered something for every theatrical taste. Whether you're discovering these productions for the first time or revisiting old favorites, this collection represents a defining moment in contemporary American theater.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2023

As we look back from March 2026, the 2023 Broadway season stands as a remarkable period for dramatic theater, marked by bold revivals and innovative new works that continue to resonate with audiences.

The year's productions average an impressive 82/100 critical score across our featured selections, reflecting a season of exceptional artistic achievement. Leading the pack is Maria Friedman's revelatory revival of **Merrily We Roll Along** (85/100), which finally unlocks the emotional power of Sondheim's former flop through inspired casting and direction. The production proves that some shows simply need time—and the right interpretation—to find their audience.

Equally compelling is **Appropriate** (83/100), Branden Jacobs-Jenkins's searing family drama that critics hail as a modern masterpiece, anchored by Sarah Paulson's commanding performance. The play's unflinching examination of inheritance, both material and moral, demonstrates the enduring power of ensemble drama. Meanwhile, **Stranger Things: The First Shadow** (85/100) brings technical wizardry to Broadway, with this West End transfer earning praise for transcending its source material through jaw-dropping stagecraft.

The season also features significant revivals like **Purlie Victorious** (82/100) and **Parade** (82/100), both proving bracingly relevant decades after their original productions, alongside innovative solo works such as **Just for Us** (81/100) and **Prima Facie** (81/100). From **Fat Ham**'s Pulitzer-winning Hamlet reimagining to Josh Groban's turn in **Sweeney Todd**, 2023 offered remarkable range.

Whether you're catching up on shows still running or exploring these productions through cast recordings and videos, these ten plays represent some of Broadway's finest dramatic work from the decade.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in March 2026

As Broadway moves through March 2026, the shows that debuted in 2024 continue to demonstrate remarkable staying power and critical acclaim. This collection of ten productions maintains an impressive average critic score of 84/100, reflecting a particularly strong season for theatrical storytelling across multiple genres.

Leading the field is **Stereophonic**, David Adjmi's acclaimed drama about a 1970s rock band, which critics consistently praise as a theatrical marvel for its authentic portrayal of the creative process. The play's meticulous attention to period detail and its exploration of artistic collaboration resonate deeply with both reviewers and audiences.

Musical theater innovation defines much of this lineup, from **Maybe Happy Ending**'s emotionally resonant robot love story—hailed as one of Broadway's most original musicals in years—to **CATS: The Jellicle Ball**, a ballroom-infused reimagining that transforms the familiar material into something entirely fresh. Meanwhile, **Operation Mincemeat** brings grassroots energy from its origins to Broadway, earning praise for its inventive ensemble work.

Comedy finds its voice through **Oh, Mary!**, Cole Escola's absurdist farce reimagining Mary Todd Lincoln as a cabaret-obsessed narcissist, which continues to earn raves for its riotous irreverence. Classic revivals also hold their own, with **Gypsy** featuring Audra McDonald's deeply moving interpretation of Mama Rose, and **Oliver!** delivering lavish production values that balance charm with Dickensian grit.

Whether you're drawn to innovative new works or fresh takes on beloved classics, these critically acclaimed productions offer compelling reasons to experience Broadway's current landscape.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in March 2026

As Broadway moves through March 2026, the season's strongest offerings—productions that opened throughout 2025—demonstrate the enduring power of both bold revivals and urgent new voices. This month's top ten plays average an impressive 84/100 from critics, reflecting a particularly strong year for dramatic work on Broadway stages.

Leading the field is Ivo van Hove's stripped-down production of **All My Sons**, which earns the highest critical marks (91/100) for its emotionally searing approach to Arthur Miller's classic. The minimalist staging allows the ensemble cast to deliver performances critics describe as devastating in their intensity. Close behind, the 20th-anniversary revival of **The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee** (90/100) proves the musical's charm remains undiminished, with reviewers celebrating its perfect balance of humor and heart.

The lineup showcases Broadway's range, from **Paddington The Musical**'s family-friendly enchantment—anchored by what critics call a remarkably lifelike puppet—to Sanaz Toossi's Pulitzer-winning **English**, which brings nuanced intelligence to questions of language and belonging. Major revivals of **Ragtime** and Arthur Miller bookend newer works like Branden Jacobs-Jenkins' **Purpose** and Jocelyn Bioh's **Liberation**, both continuing these playwrights' examinations of family, memory, and American identity.

The diversity of storytelling approaches, from van Hove's austere classicism to the vibrant spectacle of **Buena Vista Social Club**, reflects a Broadway season willing to take artistic risks while honoring theatrical tradition. Whether you're drawn to intimate character studies or sweeping musical narratives, this month's selections offer compelling reasons to experience live theater.

best-broadway-plays-2026.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2026

March 2026 brings an intimate start to the year's Broadway play offerings, with quality taking precedence over quantity in the early season.

Leading the way is **Every Brilliant Thing**, Daniel Radcliffe's critically acclaimed solo show that breaks the fourth wall between performer and audience. With an impressive 81/100 critic score across 19 reviews, this interactive meditation on depression and life's small pleasures showcases Radcliffe's considerable warmth and theatrical range beyond his film work. Critics consistently praise the production's ability to tackle heavy subject matter while celebrating everyday moments of joy, making it a standout in the current season.

The early months of 2026 suggest that Broadway is embracing smaller-scale, emotionally resonant work that prioritizes connection over spectacle. While the play selection remains limited in March, the strong critical reception for what has opened indicates that audiences are responding to thoughtful, character-driven storytelling.

As spring approaches, this initial offering sets a promising tone for the theatrical year ahead. The success of intimate productions like *Every Brilliant Thing* may signal a broader trend toward more experimental and personal work finding commercial viability on Broadway stages.

For theatergoers looking to experience the best of what's currently available, the choice is clear but rewarding—a focused season that favors depth over breadth. Check back as the year progresses to see how the 2026 Broadway play landscape evolves with new openings and extended runs.
